title: Homological functors of triangulated categories
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a pretriangulated category (with shift $[1]$,
distinguished triangles and rotation), and let $\mathcal A$ be abelian
[def-sp-abelian]. An additive functor $F:\mathcal C\to\mathcal A$ is
*homological* if for every distinguished triangle $K_1\to K_2\to K_3\to
K_1[1]$ the sequences $F(K_1)\to F(K_2)\to F(K_3)$ and $F(K_2)\to F(K_3)\to F(K_1[1])$
are exact at the middle spots.

mathlib_match.how: The class declaration at line 82 (`CategoryTheory.Functor.IsHomological`) requires zero-morphism preservation and exactness of the image under F of the short complex K_1 -> K_2 -> K_3 of every distinguished triangle: this is the first clause. The second clause, exactness of F(K_2) -> F(K_3) -> F(K_1[1]), is the same field applied to the rotated triangle, distinguished by `Pretriangulated.rot_of_distTriang` (Mathlib/CategoryTheory/Triangulated/Pretriangulated.lean:104), so it is part of the notion rather than an extra requirement. Additivity is the inferred instance at line 153 (`F.Additive` from `[F.IsHomological]`), and conversely an additive functor preserves zero morphisms; so the definition agrees with the class.
